===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁er-|id=earth}}
From {{inh|en|enm|erthe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|eorþe}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*erþu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*erþō||dirt, ground, earth}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₁er-|*h₁érteh₂|earth|id=earth}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|erd}}, {{m|sco|yerd}}, {{m|sco|yird}}, {{m|sco|yirth|t=earth, loam, mould, soil; ground}}, {{cog|yol|eard}}, {{m|yol|eart}}, {{m|yol|eord}}, {{m|yol|eorth}}, {{m|yol|erth|t=earth}}, {{cog|frr|eerd}}, {{m|frr|eerde}}, {{m|frr|iarde}}, {{m|frr|Iart}}, {{m|frr|iir}}, {{m|frr|jard}}, {{m|frr|örd}}, {{m|frr|Öört|t=earth; world}}, {{cog|stq|Idde}}, {{m|stq|Äid}}, {{m|stq|Äide|t=earth; soil; ground}}, {{cog|fy|ierde|t=earth; soil; ground}}, {{cog|gsw|Ëërde|t=earth}}, {{cog|bar|Erd}}, {{m|bar|Erdn|t=world; soil; ground}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|Ääd|t=earth}}, {{cog|cim|èerda|t=earth}}, {{cog|nl|aard}}, {{m|nl|aarde|t=earth}}, {{cog|de|Erde|t=earth; soil; ground; world}}, {{cog|nds-de|Eer|t=earth}}, {{cog|li|eerd|t=earth}}, {{cog|lb|Äerd|t=earth; soil}}, {{cog|wym|Ād|t=earth}}, {{cog|yi|ערד|t=earth; soil}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|jord|t=earth}}, {{cog|fo|jørð|t=earth}}, {{cog|is|jörð|t=earth}}, {{cog|nrn|yurn|t=the earth}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐌹𐍂𐌸𐌰|t=earth}}; also {{cog|la|ōra|t=border, edge, rim}}, {{cog|br|erv|t=ridge between furrows}}, {{cog|cy|erw|t=acre}}, {{cog|grc|ἔραζε|t=to the ground}}, {{cog|lt|erdvė|t=expanse, space}}, {{cog|sq|varr}}, {{m|sq|vorr|t=grave}}, {{cog|txb|āre|t=dust, loose earth}}, {{cog|sa|उर्वरा|t=fertile soil, field yielding crops}}, {{cog|hit|𒅕𒄩𒀸|tr=''er-ḫa-aš''|ts=erḫaš|t=border, boundary, line}}.

Probably unrelated, but of unknown etymology, is {{noncog|xcl|երկիր|t=earth}}. Likewise, the phonologically similar {{cog|sem-pro|*ʔarṣ́-}}&nbsp;– whence {{noncog|ar|أَرْض}}, {{noncog|he|אֶרֶץ|tr=ʾereṣ}}&nbsp;– is probably unrelated.
{{col-bottom}}

===Proper noun===
{{en-proper noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q2}} {{alternative case form of|en|Earth}}; our [[planet]], [[third]] out from the [[Sun]].
#: {{ux|en|The astronauts saw the '''earth''' from the porthole.}}
#* {{RQ:Conrad Heart of Darkness|page=193|passage=We live in the flicker - may it last as long as the old '''earth''' keeps rolling!}}

====Usage notes====
* The names of celestial bodies are usually capitalized ({{m|en|Earth}}), even when used with {{m|en|the}}.

====Translations====
{{trans-see|id=Q2|our planet, third out from the Sun|Earth}}

===Noun===
[[File:BrownSoil.jpg|thumb|Earth or soil ({{senseno|en|soil}})]]
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|soil}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[soil|Soil]].
#: {{ux|en|This is good '''earth''' for growing potatoes.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Any general [[rock]]-based material.
#: {{ux|en|She sighed when the plane's wheels finally touched '''earth'''.}}
# The [[ground]], [[land]] (as opposed to the [[sky]] or [[sea]]).
#: {{ux|en|Birds are of the sky, not of the '''earth'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=David Simpson
|volume=188|issue=26|page=36|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/books/2013/may/18/falling-upwards-richard-holmes-review Fantasy of navigation]
|passage=Like most human activities, ballooning has sponsored heroes and hucksters and a good deal in between. For every dedicated scientist patiently recording atmospheric pressure and wind speed while shivering at high altitudes, there is a carnival barker with a bevy of pretty girls willing to dangle from a basket or parachute down to '''earth'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q6501125}} {{lb|en|British}} A connection [[electrically]] to the ''earth'' ({{qualifier|US}} [[ground]]); on equipment: a terminal connected in that manner.
# The [[lair]] or [[den]] (as a [[hole]] in the ground) of an animal such as a fox.
# A [[region]] of the planet; a [[land]] or [[country]].
# [[worldly|Worldly]] things, as against spiritual ones.
# The [[world]] of our [[current]] [[life]] (as opposed to [[heaven]] or an [[afterlife]]).
#* {{RQ:Keats Lamia|poem=Ode on a Grecian Urn|stanza=5|page=116|passage="Beauty is truth, truth beauty,"—that is all / Ye know on '''earth''', and all ye need to know.}}
# {{lb|en|metonymically}} The [[people]] on the globe.
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Genesis|11|1|page=87|column=2|passage=And the whole '''earth''' was of one language, and of one [[speach|ſpeach]].}}
# Any [[planet]] similar to the [[Earth]] (our earth): an [[exoplanet]] viewed as another earth, or a potential one.
#: {{ux|en|New space telescopes may accelerate the search for other '''earths''' that may be out there.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} The [[human]] [[body]].{{anchor|en_noun_obschem}}
# {{lb|en|alchemy|philosophy|and|Taoism}} The aforementioned soil- or rock-based material, considered one of the {{w|Classical element|four or five classical elements}}.
# {{lb|en|chemistry|obsolete}} Any of certain substances now known to be [[oxide]]s of [[metal]], which were distinguished by being [[infusible]], and by [[insolubility]] in [[water]].
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1846|author=unspecified |title=METALS, OXIDES, EARTHS AND ALKALIES|url=https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=File:Scientific_American_-_Series_1_-_Volume_002_-_Issue_13.pdf&page=6|passage=The term '''''Earths''''' was formerly, and is still, but in a modified sense, applied to several substances which compose all the various rocks, stones, gems, mountains, and soils covering the face of the globe.  They are tasteless, inodorous, dry, uninflamable, sparingly soluble, difficult of fusion, and of moderate specific gravity.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|UK|transitive}} To connect [[electrically]] to the earth.
#: {{syn|en|ground}}
#: {{ux|en|That noise is because the amplifier is not properly '''earthed'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[bury]].
#* {{RQ:Young Night-Thoughts|328|The Miſer '''earths''' his Treaſure; and the Thief, / Watching the Mole, half-beggars him ere Morn.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[hide]], or cause to hide, in the earth; to chase into a [[burrow]] or [[den]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Spanish Fryar|48|{{...}}the Fox is '''earth’d''',{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1819|author=John Mayer|title=The Sportsman's Directory, or Park and Gamekeeper's Companion|passage=This is the time that the horseman are flung out, not having the cry to lead them to the death. When quadruped animals of the venery or hunting kind are at rest, the stag is said to be harboured, the buck lodged, the fox kennelled, the badger '''earthed''', the otter vented or watched, the hare formed, and the rabbit set.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[burrow]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1740|author=w:Thomas Tickell|title=Fragment on Hunting|passage=foxes '''earth'd'''}}
